newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals slip on long-liquidation.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals slip on long-liquidation.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended weaker on Monday, weighed down by private investors' long liquidation, following slips in spot prices in New York on Friday, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from five yen to nine yen per gram lower, with most-active benchmark October ending six yen lower at 1,325 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from flat to eight yen per gram lower, with benchmark October finishing down six at 1,335 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $368.55/369.05 per ounce at 0739 GMT, against $368.70/369.20 in New York on Friday.
In gold futures, price losses were partly offset by constant bargain-hunting buying interest in distant months.

Traders said gold remained vulnerable to the downside risks partly, because losses in the U.S stock market last Friday were limited. "Spot gold may dip further with additional producer selling looming as the short covering-led gold price rebound last Friday proved to be short-lived," one trader said.
He pegged the initial support at $366 per ounce.
In platinum futures, large long positions still held by individual investors continued to undermine sentiment, the traders said.

"I think large long positions in TOCOM were one of the main reason behind the recent bearishness in spot platinum. The platinum market could be pressured by long-liquidation until the December contract's spot expiry later this month," another trader said. Traders said there has not been much Russian selling of platinum group metals in the spot market recently after active Russian sales were detected in September and October.
Benchmark October silver futures were down 1.6 yen per 10 grams at 176.2 yen. Benchmark October palladium was flat at 422 yen. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk +81-3-3432-7431
